segments.t: Nastya challenges Kostya to suggest a better name for their baby. Kostya proposes naming the boy Dmitry, and turns to Max to ask which name sounds better. Listen to the full conversation in Russian first, and then we will walk through every line together.
Хорошо, давай, как ты хочешь назвать?
Ничего подобного, дорогая Настя.
Дмитрий — это очень красивое имя.
Ну сама внимательно смотри.
Тут Дмитрий, а тут какой-то Кузьма.
Знаешь, имя Дмитрий хотя бы звучит.
А чем тебе плохо имя Кузьма?
Честно, я даже не знаю это.
А давай сейчас у Макса спросим.
Макс, скажи, Дмитрий же лучше?
Возьмите ваш заказ, пожалуйста.
Ну, что ты нам скажешь, Макс?
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Хорошо, давай, как ты хочешь назвать?

'Alright, go ahead, what do you want to name him?' Questioning whether Alright go ahead what do Kostya wants to name him is how Nastya tests Kostya's story. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
Ничего подобного, дорогая Настя.
'Nothing of the sort, dear Nastya.' With the argument and conversation in play, Kostya keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Дмитрий — это очень красивое имя.
'Dmitry is a very handsome name.' Kostya explains that Dmitry is a very handsome name, keeping his voice calm and direct.
Ну сама внимательно смотри.
'Well look closely for yourself.' Over the argument and the conversation, Kostya answers Max without a second thought.
Тут Дмитрий, а тут какой-то Кузьма.
'Here is Dmitry, and here is some Kuzma.' Noting that here is Dmitry and here is some Kuzma keeps Kostya's side of the story simple and clear.
Знаешь, имя Дмитрий хотя бы звучит.
'You know, the name Dmitry at least sounds good.' Even though the name Dmitry at least sounds good, Kostya keeps a steady face in front of Max.
А чем тебе плохо имя Кузьма?

'And what is wrong with the name Kuzma for you?' Here asking what wrong with the name Kuzma for Kostya is shows Nastya looking for the real truth. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Честно, я даже не знаю это.
'Honestly, I do not even know that.' Saying that he does not even know is how Kostya sets the tone with Max. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
А давай сейчас у Макса спросим.
'Let us ask Max right now.' Realizing that they should ask Max right now changes how Kostya handles the situation.
Макс, скажи, Дмитрий же лучше?

'Max, tell us, Dmitry is better, right?' Wondering if tell them Dmitry is better right shows Kostya caught off guard. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Возьмите ваш заказ, пожалуйста.

'Take your order, please.' Mentioning that Kostya should take Kostya's order please moves the talk in a new direction. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Ну, что ты нам скажешь, Макс?
'Well, what will you tell us, Max?' By asking what Kostya tells them will, Nastya presses Kostya for a straight answer. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
